Electronic Health Information export1. Single patient electronic health information export.\n1. Enable a user to timely create an export file(s) with all of a single patient’s\nelectronic health information that can be stored at the time of certification by\nthe product, of which the Health IT Module is a part.\n2. The encrypted PHI data is stored on the\n    58→ASP/Client server.\n    59→Data Filles exported :\n    60→• Includes EHI that can be stored at the time of certification by the product\n    61→• Are in electronic and in a computable format\n    62→• Includes a publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format\n    63→\n    64→\fSingle Patient Data Export\n    65→Benchmark EHR User with , CuresEHIExport’’ role can export Single Patient EHI any time\n    66→\n    67→the user chooses and without subsequent developer assistance to operate.\n    68→User Role, CuresEHIExport is present under the Role (No Access Rights) section of the\n    69→User Role Master screen in Benchmark EHR.\n    70→The CuresEHIExport User Role must be checked for a Provider, Medical Assistant, Office\n    71→Staff or Clinical Staff user to enable the user to export data for Single Patient on Export\n    72→Patient Data popup without password or any intervention.\n    73→When a user assigned with CuresEHIExport User Role logs into Benchmark EHR the Data\n    74→Export link is available, the Single Patient radio button is selected by default for such\n    75→user.\n    76→Other enabled options on the popup include:\n    77→• Include Deleted Encounters (Use with caution)\n    78→• Reason for Data Export\n    79→• Check All and other listed checkboxes\n    80→• CONFIGURE\n    81→• CANCEL\n    82→• EXPORT\n    83→Disabled options on the popup include:\n    84→• All Patients\n    85→• Selected Patients\n    86→• Patients of Primary Provider\n    87→• Patients of Attending Provider\n    88→• Encounters of Attending Provider\n    89→• Patient Last name From-Upto\n    90→• Data Export for Patient from SQL file\n    91→• Encounter Date Range From and Upto\n    92→• Data Export Password\n    93→Clicking on the Search icon invokes Patients Search List with Active Patients in\n    94→Benchmark EHR. On selecting a Patient from this popup, the name of the Patient is\n    95→shown in the grayed-out text field. A message is displayed beside the Search icon of this\n    96→field all the time. This message reads: (For All/Multiple Patients Data Export, please\n    97→contact Bizmatics Support Team)\n    98→\n    99→\fUser can select the checkboxes for the Type of Data to be exported and click on the\n   100→EXPORT button. As Data Export Password field is disabled for the user with\n   101→CuresEHIExport User Role assigned to them, validation to Enter Password is not shown\n   102→on click of the EXPORT button. Instead, a confirmation message is directly shown in a\n   103→popup which reads: The Patient Data Export will be generated in the Background. User\n   104→will be notified on mail when the report is generated. Click on the OK button to close\n   105→the confirmation popup.\n   106→Download Files :\n   107→Single Patient Data is exported under ‘Download Files’\n   108→Navigate to Settings → Configuration → Clinic column → Download Files\n   109→A Category Cures EHI Export is present on the Download Files Master screen on the\n   110→EMR side. The record for a file downloaded on exporting Single Patients is shown here.\n   111→Files shown under this Category are of the .zip format. The Comment column of the\n   112→record shows ‘EHI Export’. On clicking the file hyperlink, a zip folder is downloaded in\n   113→user’s local Downloads folder. The downloaded zip folder contains exported data in .txt,\n   114→.xls and .pdf formats.\n   115→\n   116→Patient Population (All/Multiple) Data Export\n   117→Patient Population Data Export is handled by Bizmatics Data Migration Team as it\n   118→depends on size of data ,time and efforts required to manage the server resources\n   119→Please contact Bizmatics Customer Support Team at support@bizmaticsinc.com to\n   120→initiate the process.\n   121→\n   122→Audit Trail\n   123→Single Patient and Patient Population Data Export action can be tracked in Audit Trail\n   124→Reports\n   125→\n   126→\fAPPENDIX\n   127→DATA FORMATS\n   128→For Single or Patient Population encrypted Data Files/Folders are exported in following formats:\n   129→•\n   130→\n   131→PHI without any documents attached, data is exported in xls and .txt format\n   132→o\n   133→\n   134→•\n   135→\n   136→For example, for Allergy:\n   137→Exported field list is - Last name, First name, Middle name, Chart no, Account no,\n   138→Birth date, Allergy, Reaction, Type, Int Name, Status,Rxnorm\n   139→\n   140→PHI with documents attached, for example Lab Results, Rad Results, Old Progress\n   141→Notes, Results, Letters, etc. the xls contains a specific column labeled “File” which\n   142→contains the path of the respective document.\n   143→For example, for Letters:\n   144→Exported field list is - Last name, First name, Middle name, Chart no, Account no,\n   145→Birth date, Letter Date, Outward (O) Inward (I), To Name, Subject, List of To\n   146→Names, List of Cc Names, List of To and Cc Names, Status Code, Status Name,\n   147→FILE\n   148→For ex. Certification Program’ criteria –\n§170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information export’\nONC Compliance Date: Dec 31,2023\n\n2015 Edition Cures Update Certification Requirements:\n§ 170.315 (b)(10) Electronic Health Information export1. Single patient electronic health information export.\n1. Enable a user to timely create an export file(s) with all of a single patient’s\nelectronic health information that can be stored at the time of certification by\nthe product, of which the Health IT Module is a part.\n2. A user must be able to execute this capability at any time the user chooses and\nwithout subsequent developer assistance to operate.\n3. Limit the ability of users who can create such export file(s) in at least one of\nthese two ways:\n1. To a specific set of identified users\n2. As system administrator function.\n4. The export file(s) created must be electronic and in a computable format.\n5. The publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format must be included with\nthe exported file(s).\n\n\f2. Patient population electronic health information export. Create an export of all the\nelectronic health information that can be stored at the time of certification by the\nproduct, of which the Health IT Module is a part.\n1. The export created must be electronic and in a computable format.\n2. The publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format must be included with\nthe exported file(s).\n\n3. Documentation. The export format(s) used to support paragraphs (b)(10)(i) and (ii) of\nthis section must be kept up-to-date.\n\nBenchmark EHR Workflow\nSingle Patient Data Export :\nA Benchmark EHR user can perform an electronic health information (EHI) export for a Single\nPatient at any time the user chooses without developer assistance, can limit a set of users the\nability to perform the export.\nPatient population EHI Export :\nPatient Population Data Export is handled by Bizmatics Data Migration Team as it depends on\nsize of data, time and efforts required to manage the server resources.\nThe Data Migration Team monitors the progress of the process. The process completion\nnotification is sent to Bizmatics Data Migration Team. The encrypted PHI data is stored on the\nASP/Client server.\nData Filles exported :\n• Includes EHI that can be stored at the time of certification by the product\n• Are in electronic and in a computable format\n• Includes a publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format\n\n\fSingle Patient Data Export\nBenchmark EHR User with , CuresEHIExport’’ role can export Single Patient EHI any time\n\nthe user chooses and without subsequent developer assistance to operate.\nUser Role, CuresEHIExport is present under the Role (No Access Rights) section of the\nUser Role Master screen in Benchmark EHR.\nThe CuresEHIExport User Role must be checked for a Provider, Medical Assistant, Office\nStaff or Clinical Staff user to enable the user to export data for Single Patient on Export\nPatient Data popup without password or any intervention.\nWhen a user assigned with CuresEHIExport User Role logs into Benchmark EHR the Data\nExport link is available, the Single Patient radio button is selected by default for such\nuser.\nOther enabled options on the popup include:\n• Include Deleted Encounters (Use with caution)\n• Reason for Data Export\n• Check All and other listed checkboxes\n• CONFIGURE\n• CANCEL\n• EXPORT\nDisabled options on the popup include:\n• All Patients\n• Selected Patients\n• Patients of Primary Provider\n• Patients of Attending Provider\n• Encounters of Attending Provider\n• Patient Last name From-Upto\n• Data Export for Patient from SQL file\n• Encounter Date Range From and Upto\n• Data Export Password\nClicking on the Search icon invokes Patients Search List with Active Patients in\nBenchmark EHR. On selecting a Patient from this popup, the name of the Patient is\nshown in the grayed-out text field. A message is displayed beside the Search icon of this\nfield all the time. This message reads: (For All/Multiple Patients Data Export, please\ncontact Bizmatics Support Team)\n\n\fUser can select the checkboxes for the Type of Data to be exported and click on the\nEXPORT button. As Data Export Password field is disabled for the user with\nCuresEHIExport User Role assigned to them, validation to Enter Password is not shown\non click of the EXPORT button. Instead, a confirmation message is directly shown in a\npopup which reads: The Patient Data Export will be generated in the Background. User\nwill be notified on mail when the report is generated. Click on the OK button to close\nthe confirmation popup.\nDownload Files :\nSingle Patient Data is exported under ‘Download Files’\nNavigate to Settings → Configuration → Clinic column → Download Files\nA Category Cures EHI Export is present on the Download Files Master screen on the\nEMR side. The record for a file downloaded on exporting Single Patients is shown here.\nFiles shown under this Category are of the .zip format. The Comment column of the\nrecord shows ‘EHI Export’. On clicking the file hyperlink, a zip folder is downloaded in\nuser’s local Downloads folder. The downloaded zip folder contains exported data in .txt,\n.xls and .pdf formats.\n\nPatient Population (All/Multiple) Data Export\nPatient Population Data Export is handled by Bizmatics Data Migration Team as it\ndepends on size of data ,time and efforts required to manage the server resources\nPlease contact Bizmatics Customer Support Team at support@bizmaticsinc.com to\ninitiate the process.\n\nAudit Trail\nSingle Patient and Patient Population Data Export action can be tracked in Audit Trail\nReports\n\n\fAPPENDIX\nDATA FORMATS\nFor Single or Patient Population encrypted Data Files/Folders are exported in following formats:\n•\n\nPHI without any documents attached, data is exported in xls and .txt format\no\n\n•\n\nFor example, for Allergy:\nExported field list is - Last name, First name, Middle name, Chart no, Account no,\nBirth date, Allergy, Reaction, Type, Int Name, Status,Rxnorm\n\nPHI with documents attached, for example Lab Results, Rad Results, Old Progress\nNotes, Results, Letters, etc. the xls contains a specific column labeled “File” which\ncontains the path of the respective document.\nFor example, for Letters:\nExported field list is - Last name, First name, Middle name, Chart no, Account no,\nBirth date, Letter Date, Outward (O) Inward (I), To Name, Subject, List of To\nNames, List of Cc Names, List of To and Cc Names, Status Code, Status Name,\nFILE\nFor ex. CHART01/LETOut_99.pdf CHART01/LETIn_389.pdf\nHere, CHART01 is the folder and the LETOut_99 and LETIn_389 corresponds\nto the physical file stored under the Folder CHART01.\n\n•\n\nCCD Export: This includes Consolidated Cures CCD and data element xls includes\ncolumn HTML, XML which contains path of that document.\nExported field list is - - Last name, First name, Middle name, Chart no, Account\nno, Birth date, DOC_ID, Date, Provider, HTML, XML\n\n\fData Elements Types\nUser can select Data Elements to be exported from following list:\n\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n\nInsurance Master\nMedics\nReferring Provider\nAdjusters\nAttorneys\nEmployers\nGuarantor\nPatient Demographics\nPatient Insurance\nVaccination\nHealth Maintenance\nFamily History\nPast Medical Hist\nSurgery\nAllergy\nCurrent Medication\nSocial History\nLegal Documents\nOther Documents\nEnc Attach Docs\nOld Progress Notes\n\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n\nMessages\nFuture Appointments\nVitals\nDiagnosis Codes\nCPT Codes\nHcpc Codes\nCCD\nPrescriptions\nLab Results\nRad Results\nProcedure Orders\nConsults\nEnc Progress Notes\nProcedure Notes\nLetters\nAll Vitals\nLab Test Result Values\nPatient Cases\nPatient Notes\nPatient Alert\nPast Appointments\n\nWhen Billing is turned on for the clinic then the following options are also shown •\n•\n•\n•\n•\n\nBilling Ledger\nBilling Claims\nBilling Charges\nPatient Advance\nStatements\n\n\f§170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information export_Self Attestation Document\n\nDetailed Description of the Data Export Contents\n1. It is a genuine (b)(10) export documentation — not a repackaged FHIR/(g)(10) document.\n\n### Export Mechanism\n\nThe export is a **proprietary database dump** delivered as a ZIP file containing:\n- **XLS (Excel)** files for structured/tabular data\n- **TXT** files for text data\n- **PDF** files for documents and attachments (progress notes, letters, legal documents, etc.)\n- **HTML/XML** files for CCD (Consolidated Clinical Document) data\n\nThere are two export modes:\n1. **Single Patient Export**: Self-service via the EHR UI. Users with the `CuresEHIExport` role can select a patient, choose data element types via checkboxes, and trigger an async background export. The ZIP is available under Settings → Configuration → Download Files → \"Cures EHI Export\" category.\n2. **Patient Population Export**: Not self-service — requires contacting the \"Bizmatics Data Migration Team\" at support@bizmaticsinc.com. This is described as resource-intensive and managed by the vendor. (Note: \"Bizmatics\" appears to be the development/services entity behind Benchmark.)\n\n### Data Elements (47 categories)\n\nThe export covers **47 data element types**, each documented with a description and most with explicit database column-level field lists. The 42 core (non-billing) elements are always available; the 5 billing elements appear only \"when Billing is turned on for the clinic\":\n\n**Clinical data (core EHR):**\n- Patient Demographics (131 fields — extremely detailed including race, ethnicity, language, sexual orientation, gender identity)\n- Patient Insurance (62 fields)\n- Vaccination records\n- Health Maintenance\n- Family History\n- Past Medical History\n- Surgery history\n- Allergies (with RxNorm and NDC codes)\n- Current Medications (with NDC and RxNorm codes)\n- Social History (with SNOMED and LOINC codes)\n- Vitals / All Vitals (with SNOMED and LOINC codes)\n- Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10, with assessment and plan notes)\n- CPT Codes (with SNOMED codes and IMO descriptions)\n- HCPC Codes\n- Prescriptions (complete Rx history)\n- Lab Results and Lab Test Result Values (discrete results with LOINC codes)\n- Radiology Results\n- Procedure Orders\n- Consults\n- Encounter Progress Notes (closed encounters, with extensive provider/referee fields)\n- Procedure Notes\n- CCD (Consolidated Clinical Document as HTML+XML)\n\n**Documents and correspondence:**\n- Legal Documents (as PDF)\n- Other Documents (as PDF)\n- Encounter Attached Documents (as PDF)\n- Old Progress Notes (as PDF)\n- Letters (inward/outward, consolidated PDF)\n- Messages (patient messages)\n\n**Administrative/reference data:**\n- Insurance Master (insurance company reference data)\n- Medics (provider/staff reference)\n- Referring Providers\n- Adjusters, Attorneys, Employers, Guarantors\n- Patient Cases (workers' comp, injury cases)\n- Patient Notes, Patient Alerts\n- Future Appointments, Past Appointments\n\n**Billing data (when billing module enabled):**\n- Billing Ledger\n- Billing Claims (185 fields — extremely detailed CMS 1500 claim data)\n- Billing Charges (line-level charge detail)\n- Patient Advance (advance payments)\n- Statements (rendered as PDF)\n\n### Field-Level Detail\n\nThe documentation provides **1,146 explicitly named database column fields** across the 36 entities that have quoted field lists. Column naming follows a consistent `PREFIX_FIELDNAME` convention (e.g., `PT_FNAME`, `BLH_CLAIM_STATUS`, `LOD_TEST_LOINC`). This is essentially a flattened view of the underlying database schema.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is an **unusually thorough (b)(10) export** that covers substantially all data domains identified in the product research:\n\n**Clearly covered:**\n- Demographics, contacts, insurance/enrollment ✓ (extensive — 131 demographic fields, 62 insurance fields)\n- Diagnoses, problem lists ✓ (ICD-10, SNOMED, assessment notes)\n- Medications and prescriptions ✓ (current meds + full prescription history, with RxNorm/NDC)\n- Lab results ✓ (both order-level and discrete test result values with LOINC)\n- Radiology results ✓\n- Vital signs ✓ (per-encounter and all-encounters, with LOINC/SNOMED)\n- Allergies ✓ (with RxNorm, NDC, adverse event, SNOMED reaction codes)\n- Immunization records ✓ (CVX codes, manufacturer, lot, route, site)\n- Procedures and surgical history ✓\n- Clinical notes (progress notes, procedure notes) ✓ (as PDF exports from encounters)\n- Letters and correspondence ✓\n- Consults and referrals ✓\n- Family history ✓ (with SNOMED)\n- Social history ✓ (with SNOMED and LOINC)\n- Patient messages ✓\n- Billing records ✓ (claims, charges, ledger, advance payments, statements — 185 fields for claims alone)\n- Patient cases (workers' comp, injury) ✓\n- Documents and attachments ✓ (legal, other, encounter-attached, old progress notes)\n- CCD (C-CDA documents) ✓\n- Care team / provider reference data ✓ (medics, referring providers, with NPI/taxonomy)\n- Appointments ✓ (future and past)\n\n**Potentially missing or ambiguous:**\n- **Care plans / goals**: Not explicitly listed as a separate export category. Care plan data may be embedded in progress notes or CCD documents, but there's no dedicated \"Care Plans\" entity.\n- **Patient education materials distributed**: The product research notes MedlinePlus education materials are distributed to patients. No explicit export for this.\n- **Patient intake forms**: Mentioned as a portal feature; no explicit export for intake form responses as structured data (though they may be captured in encounter documents).\n- **Custom specialty templates**: The product supports 40+ specialty templates for notes, but the export captures the rendered notes (as PDFs), not the structured template field data.\n\nThese gaps are minor. The export covers the core clinical record, billing records, and documents comprehensively.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **proprietary format** — not FHIR, C-CDA, or any interoperability standard. It is essentially a **database dump in Excel/text files with associated PDF documents**, organized by data element type.\n\nThis is an appropriate format for (b)(10). The export is clearly computable (XLS, TXT files), and for documents that are inherently rendered (progress notes, letters, legal documents), PDF is a reasonable format. The inclusion of CCD HTML/XML exports adds a layer of standards-based clinical summary alongside the raw data.\n\nThe format is **not self-describing**: there are no embedded data types, value set definitions, or schema files in the export. A consumer would need this PDF document to understand the column names and their meanings. However, the column naming convention is largely self-explanatory (e.g., `PT_DOB` = patient date of birth, `BLH_BILL_AMOUNT` = billing amount).\n\nRelationships between entities are implicit through shared ID fields (e.g., `PT_ID`, `BLH_ENC_ID`, `LOH_DOC_ID`) but not formally documented as foreign keys. A developer importing this data would need to infer relationships from column naming patterns.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- **Field-level granularity**: 1,146 named fields across 47 entities — this is unusually detailed for (b)(10) documentation\n- **Comprehensive scope**: 47 data element types covering clinical, administrative, and billing domains\n- **Consistent format**: Each entity has a numbered description, export notes, and a quoted field list\n- **Practical export instructions**: Clear description of the CuresEHIExport role, UI workflow, and where to find downloaded files\n- **Honest about limitations**: Notes which data is excluded (inactive records, void claims, UB04 forms, deleted encounters)\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **No data type information**: Fields are listed by name only — no column data types (string, date, integer, boolean), lengths, or constraints\n- **No value set documentation**: Fields like `PT_MARITAL_STATUS`, `TEI_STATUS_NAME`, `BLH_CLAIM_STATUS` use coded values that are not defined\n- **No relationship documentation**: No foreign key or entity-relationship documentation\n- **No sample data**: No example export files or sample records\n- **Population export requires vendor assistance**: The bulk export is not self-service, potentially creating an information blocking concern since it depends on the \"Bizmatics Data Migration Team\"\n- **Boolean fields undocumented**: Many `BOOL_*` fields (e.g., `PT_BOOL_SELFPAY`, `BLH_BOOL_WORK_COMP`) with no explanation of what true/false means\n- **Original URL is dead**: The live URL returns 403; the document was only retrievable via Wayback Machine\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation is moderately granular:\n- Entity-level: 47 named entities with descriptions ✓\n- Field-level: database column names for 36 of 47 entities ✓\n- Data types: Not documented ✗\n- Value sets/codes: Not documented (except noting which standard code systems are used: ICD-10, SNOMED, LOINC, CVX, RxNorm, NDC) ✗\n- Relationships: Not formally documented ✗\n- Examples: None ✗\n- Versioning: Document is version \"Denali 3.1\", no change history ✗\n\nA developer could identify what data is included in an export from this documentation, but could not fully reconstruct the patient record without additional context about data types, value sets, and inter-entity relationships.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nBenchmark EHR's (b)(10) export documentation is **above average** for the EHR market. The vendor has clearly invested effort in documenting a genuine EHI export that goes well beyond USCDI/US Core. The 47 data element types cover clinical, administrative, billing, and document data — this is a proper designated record set export, not a repackaged FHIR API.\n\nThe export is a proprietary database dump format, which is pragmatic: it exports more data than any standardized format would easily accommodate, and the field naming convention makes most columns self-explanatory. The main documentation gaps are in data types, value sets, and relationships — the sort of metadata that would be present in a formal schema definition.\n\nThe population-level export requiring vendor contact (Bizmatics Data Migration Team) is a compliance concern for the (b)(10)(ii) requirement, which calls for creating a bulk export without specifying it must be self-service — but the spirit of the regulation suggests it should be available without dependency on the vendor's schedule.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Registered URL: https://www.benchmarksystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/b-10-EHI-Export_Benchmark-Support_Self-Attestation-Document_final-1.pdf\n- Final URL (after redirect): https://web.archive.org/web/20240220215439/https://www.benchmarksystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/b-10-EHI-Export_Benchmark-Support_Self-Attestation-Document_final-1.pdf\n- Status: found (via Wayback Machine; live URL returns 403)\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (once accessible)\n- Anti-bot issues: Entire benchmarksystems.com domain returns 403; appears to be a hosting/CDN block\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n1. **Live URL returns 403**: The registered CHPL URL and the entire benchmarksystems.com domain return HTTP 403 Forbidden.
